transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I guess what started as just eating cleaner to get in shape for the lieutenant track at the firehouse has turned into something else. I've been cutting my meals way down. Lately, it's just been things like black coffee, a protein shake, and a really small dinner. And I'm doing that even on shift days, when I know for a fact I've burned way more than what I'm taking in. So, I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Besides cutting down on how much you eat, are you doing anything else to try to control your weight or burn off calories—like exercising a lot, or anything after you do eat?

No, not really. I mean, my job is already pretty physical, so I'm getting a lot of exercise just being at work and doing drills and all that. But I'm not doing extra workouts on top of it, and I don't do anything after I eat, like throwing up or anything like that. It's really just the restricting part.
How long has this pattern of restricting your meals been going on?

I'm not exactly sure on the timeline, to be honest. It's been a while, but I couldn't give you a specific date or anything when it started getting to this point. It just kind of gradually became my normal routine.

What does your weight look like right now compared to what it was before you started restricting your food intake? Have you lost a significant amount of weight, or has your weight stayed about the same?

Yeah, I've definitely lost a good amount of weight. I notice it mostly because my gear and my station clothes just... they hang a lot looser on me now. We actually had a fitness review at the firehouse recently, and they flagged my weight as being too low for my build. But honestly, even after hearing that, part of me still feels like I should keep trimming down a little more.
